definitions.explanation: A category or style of something.
A container used to give shape to something.
A set form or sequence of movements in martial arts.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{型|かた}のスマホが{出|で}た。
examples.english: A new model of smartphone came out.

examples.japanese: この{車|くるま}は{旧型|きゅうがた}だが、まだよく{走|はし}る。
examples.english: This car is an old model, but it still runs well.

examples.japanese: ケーキの{型|かた}を{買|か}った。
クッキーの{型|かた}で{生地|きじ}を{抜|ぬ}く。
examples.english: To cut out dough with a cookie cutter.

examples.japanese: {鋳型|いがた}に{金属|きんぞく}を{流|なが}し{込|こ}む。
examples.english: To pour metal into a mold.

examples.japanese: {型|かた}の{練習|れんしゅう}をする。
{柔道|じゅうどう}では{型|かた}を{通|とお}して{技|わざ}を{身|み}につける。
examples.english: In judo, you learn techniques through practicing kata.

notes:
{型|かた} has multiple related meanings: type/model, mold/form, and pattern (martial arts).

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
- {血液型|けつえきがた}: blood type
- {新型|しんがた}: new model
- {旧型|きゅうがた}: old model
- {型紙|かたがみ}: pattern (sewing)
- {大型|おおがた}: large size/type
- {小型|こがた}: small size/type

AS SUFFIX:
〜{型|がた} indicates "type" or "model": A{型|がた} (Type A).

MARTIAL ARTS:
{型|かた} (kata) is a set sequence of movements for training in karate, judo, etc.

IDIOM:
{型|かた}にはまる: to be conventional, to follow a set pattern.
